classes.label: Area
classes.description: A top-level folder of the project.

classes.label: File
classes.description: A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).

classes.label: Type
classes.description: A class, record, struct, interface or enum defined in a file.

classes.label: Run mode
classes.description: A way to start the program, picked by its first argument.

classes.label: Sub-command
classes.description: A sub-command of a command-line parser.

classes.label: Dispatch table
classes.description: A switch or mapping that turns an operation name into the code that handles it.

classes.label: Operation
classes.description: One named operation of a dispatch table.

classes.label: HTTP route
classes.description: An HTTP endpoint the program serves.

classes.label: MCP tool
classes.description: A tool the program offers to AI clients over MCP.

classes.label: Environment variable
classes.description: An environment variable the code reads or sets (operating-system variables are left out).

classes.label: Port
classes.description: A network port number found in an address or a port setting.

classes.label: Package
classes.description: A third-party package the project declares or imports.

classes.label: External host
classes.description: A host name found in a URL.

classes.label: Command-line tool
classes.description: A well-known program the project's scripts start; it has to be installed.

classes.label: Person
classes.description: An author in the Git history.

relations.label: contains
relations.description: Project → area → file.

relations.label: defines
relations.description: The file holds the definition.

relations.label: imports
relations.description: Import or include statement.

relations.label: uses
relations.description: The code names a type defined in the other file; a run mode uses a type.

relations.label: takes as a dependency
relations.description: Constructor parameter of that type.

relations.label: extends
relations.description: Base class or implemented interface.

relations.label: loads
relations.description: A page loads a script or stylesheet.

relations.label: runs
relations.description: A script or configuration starts the other file.

relations.label: refers to
relations.description: A string in the file is the other file's path.

relations.label: references
relations.description: Project reference in a build file.

relations.label: documents
relations.description: A document links to the file or shows the operation in an example.

relations.label: serves
relations.description: A run mode passes requests to the dispatch table.

relations.label: exposes
relations.description: A run mode registers the HTTP route.

relations.label: has operation
relations.description: Key of the dispatch table.

relations.label: is handled by
relations.description: The file that holds the handler the table calls.

relations.label: calls
relations.description: The file asks for the operation by name (over HTTP, a process or in-process).

relations.label: invokes
relations.description: An MCP tool runs the operation.

relations.label: forwards to
relations.description: An HTTP route hands the request to the dispatch table.

relations.label: reads
relations.description: The file reads the environment variable.

relations.label: sets
relations.description: The file sets the environment variable.

relations.label: mentions
relations.description: The host or port appears in the file.

relations.label: depends on
relations.description: The file declares or imports the package.

relations.label: starts
relations.description: The file starts the command-line tool.

relations.label: has commits in
relations.description: Author in the Git history of the project.

model_summary.summary: Creates isolated fixtures to exercise recursive project scanning, authentication, shared references, run queue and lease behavior, delegation, and two connected device clients. It launches PlayBook server and client processes, checks their HTTP and MCP behavior, and uses a deterministic provider fixture for model-process checks.

model_summary.summary: Implements a deterministic provider process for harness wiring checks without calling a model. It reports fixture version or authentication status, otherwise reads the harness prompt, checks provider arguments and trial tool restrictions, and returns fixture data.

entities.name: scripts/fixtures/provider.py
entities.summary: Deterministic CLI fixture; not a real model/authentication test.

model_summary.summary: Implements a deterministic CLI provider fixture without calling a model or checking real authentication. It reports fixture version or login status, otherwise checks the prompt context and emits a fixed result; a wait prompt makes the process sleep for 120 seconds.

The shown code also serves as the foundation for project selection and the local dashboard API, with analysis state and snapshots stored under the PlayBook data directory.

entities.name: scripts/graphify-smoke.py
entities.summary: Real Graphify/PlayBook integration checks, using an isolated ledger and source.

model_summary.summary: Runs isolated integration checks for Graphify extraction, ontology feed generation and sync, the local dashboard, and Graphify and PlayBook MCP tools. It uses a temporary project and ledger, checks that failed analysis preserves the previous snapshot, and writes results to `artifacts/graphify-smoke-results.json`.

This page lets a user select a PlayBook project, generate or refresh its code graph, sync a graph summary to the ontology, and search the graph. It displays analysis status, graph and summary counts, provenance, and links to the graph and report; its client code calls local API endpoints for these actions.

entities.name: scripts/harness-smoke.py
entities.summary: Harness proposal/trial/adoption tests on isolated SQLite and real worker/provider processes.
